title: Make the framework describe itself accurately in the five places it doesn't

history.detail:
PASS: PASS — round 1. Audited a2fc8e3 with bookkeeping 62b68a4, main checkout. Sprint file read fresh. Working tree clean apart from the known .vscode file.

Every requirement met. The one I went at hardest was Req 5, because it promotes a claim I flagged twice and carried as an open item — and the evidence for it turned out to be real and recorded.

================================================================
REQ 5 — MY OWN CARRIED ITEM, AND IT CLOSES FOR npm
================================================================

I raised this in sprint 17 ("does `Bash(npm publish *)` match a bare `npm publish`?"), carried it through sprint 18, where the comment correctly said "Confirmed: git. Inferred, not established: npm." Sprint 20 promotes npm. That is exactly the shape of the error this epic keeps making, so I went looking for the evidence rather than reading the citation.

It exists, and it is recorded in sprint 18's own LiveQA verdict:
    claude -p --permission-mode acceptEdits --allowedTools "Bash(npm pack *)"
    task: run exactly `npm pack`, nothing appended, no arguments, no redirect
    RESULT: permission_denials 0, and bare-verb-probe-1.0.0.tgz was produced
And LiveQA's own reasoning about it is the part that makes it evidence rather than an absence: "The tarball is the part that matters: it proves the bare command actually RAN, rather than merely not being denied."

That answers sprint 18's own explicit warning — its file says "Zero denials get read as a working bound" was a named risk, and LiveQA had previously refused to score zero denials as evidence for exactly that reason. This probe does not rest on zero denials; it produces a positive artifact proving execution. Correct method, correctly reasoned, and it closes the question for npm.

The promotion is also correctly bounded, which the criterion asks about specifically: "Confirmed: git and npm. Inferred, not established: every other entry on this list -- promoting these two is not license to claim the general property." Exactly one entry promoted, general caveat intact. My carried item narrows to "every entry other than git and npm remains inferred" and stays on the list in that form.

================================================================
REQ 4 — MET, AND IT IS THE BEST THING IN THIS SPRINT
================================================================

The criterion says a method without its failure history reads as obvious and gets skipped. The paragraph names both prior wrong conclusions by sprint number (17 and 19), explains the mechanism of the error rather than just the fact of it — the role refused on its own judgement before the permission layer was ever consulted, and an honest reasoned refusal looks identical to an unobservable bound from outside — credits both reports as honest about what they found, gives the working method, and closes with "a method stated without this history reads as obviously correct and gets skipped by whoever tries it next."

That last clause is the criterion's own test, answered in the artifact. This is the second time this project has written down not just a correction but why the wrong version was believable, and it is the more useful half.

(My first grep missed the sprint numbers because they sit mid-paragraph rather than at line start. My tooling, not an omission — recording that because I nearly reported Req 4 as half-met on the strength of a bad grep.)

================================================================
REQS 1, 2, 3 — MET
================================================================

Req 1 — read cold against the standard that matters. LiveQA is now defined by function: "verify the released artifact in a real environment, after distribution — not a diff, not a promise, the actual thing." A project with no deployed product knows what to do: install the published package fresh into a scratch directory. The refusals the criterion names are intact and not softened — "You do NOT trust QA1's static pass, or anyone's 'it works.' You re-verify live, every time," and "you don't speculate, you don't theorize about the code." The browser is now the common case rather than the definition, in both the persona and the role table.

Req 2 — the contradiction is gone. The old text claimed LiveQA's gate did not apply to this repository. The new text states what the code actually does: cmd_complete refuses to close any sprint without a recorded LiveQA PASS, with no override. I checked the code rather than the claim — the enforcement is at sprint_lifecycle.py:1356, `if state["groundtruth_result"] != "PASS"`. (The sprint file cites :688, which is where it lived when the requirement was written; the line has moved, the enforcement has not.) Grepped the whole of CLAUDE.md for any remaining "does not apply" or skippable-gate language: none.
Worth recording what this unblocks: every sprint file since sprint 3 has carried a "LiveQA's gate is REDEFINED, not skipped" header specifically because CLAUDE.md said the opposite. That workaround is now unnecessary — which is what the Req 1 criterion is pointing at when it says the fourteen header paragraphs become unnecessary.

Req 3 — read as a consumer inside an installed target, which is the criterion's instruction. It cannot be read as licensing edits to their own scripts: "If you did not clone `fully-completely` itself to work on the framework — if you ran `npx fully-completely` or an equivalent installer into your own project — this whole section is not about you or your `scripts/`," and it redirects them to the section that does apply. It also names the near-miss rather than fixing it silently.
Verified in the actual installed artifact rather than in the source, since that is where the misreading happened: installed a fresh copy from this build into a scratch directory and confirmed the disambiguating clause is present in the target's own CLAUDE.md. The correction reaches the reader who needed it.

REQS 6, 7 — package.json 0.1.21, one line. No test files touched, which is correct for a prose-only sprint and is what Req 7 asked for rather than a gap. Ran everything: 171 OK, ALL LAUNCHER TESTS PASSED; ALL SMOKE TESTS PASSED; ALL WORKTREE TESTS PASSED; verify-tarball.sh PASSED, "Installed 0.1.21 (first install)".

================================================================
INFORMATIONAL
================================================================

1. Now that Req 2 removes the contradiction, the "LiveQA's gate is REDEFINED, not skipped" header on
   every in-flight sprint file is redundant. Not this sprint's to remove and not a defect — but the
   next sprint file written should probably not carry it, and Master Controller may want to say so
   once rather than have it copied forward out of habit.
2. Carried, unchanged: every allowlist entry other than git and npm remains inferred (narrowed this
   sprint, not closed); the CLI-version-drift item, still the strongest-evidenced open item and still
   unscheduled; the empty-string ownedRepository declaration falling through silently; the --agents
   argv budget against Windows' 32,767-char limit.

RECOMMENDATION

Ship it. /sprint-dev-done 20, then Pipeman ships and publishes 0.1.21, then `verify-publish 20`.

Committing the build before the bookkeeping this time, deliberately, after last sprint's slip — noted and correct.

Worth saying once: this sprint corrected five self-descriptions, and three of them were things a downstream reader or a downstream team would have acted on. The one that nearly caused real damage — the own-tooling section read from inside an installed copy — is now verified fixed in the installed copy rather than in the source, which is the only place that check means anything.
